Nowy Wisnicz Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nowy Wiśnicz, Poland

Not demolished. Jews first settled in Nowy Wiśnicz in the 17th century; by 1921, 1,812 residents (48%) were mostly murdered at Bełżec in 1942. This cemetery, likely founded at the start of the 17th century and first documented June 14, 1641, served not just Nowy Wiśnicz but surrounding villages including Lipnice, Łapanów, Sobolowo, Zbydniowo, and (from 1872) Bochnia. Rebbe Naftaly Rubin was buried here in 1939, and Eleazar Rubin, killed by Germans, in 1949. A 1959 asphalt factory and construction depot took over part of the grounds; Poland formally closed the cemetery in 1964. Abush and Josef Hirsch led restoration efforts in the early 1980s, removing the asphalt factory, erecting a Holocaust memorial, rebuilding the local ohel, and re-fencing the site.
